title: Walter Greene: diabetes, heart failure and a dinner club
description: 72-year-old retired janitor with uncontrolled type 2 diabetes, heart failure, hypertension and CKD stage 3, sent for medical nutrition therapy. Grumpy and sarcastic at first; opens up when he feels respected. Hidden safety issue: he takes ibuprofen for back pain.

profile.name: Walter Greene
profile.summary: Adapted from the event-provided VHS profile. Values corrected where the profile contradicted itself (see consistency findings on the imported version).

personality.summary: Cynical and sarcastic; masks fear with humor and grumpiness. Hates being pitied or treated like a child. Talks a lot once engaged.
personality.communication_style: Short and snappy at first, teases students about looking young. Warms up and jokes when listened to.
example_lines: Fine. What do you want to know?

briefing.reason_for_visit: Referral for medical nutrition therapy: diabetes, heart failure and kidney disease
briefing.goal: Take a nutrition-focused history, find what gets in the way of his eating and medicines, and agree on one or two realistic changes.

facts.text: Complains right away that all his pills make him feel dumb and nauseous.
facts.say: I take all these pills and they make me feel dumb and sick to my stomach.

facts.text: Came because his doctor sent him; does not like being sent to the clinic for diet stuff.
facts.say: My doctor sent me. I don't see what a diet talk is gonna do.

facts.text: Jokes that the student looks young.
facts.say: You look like a kid. Do I need to fill out a form for this diet thing?

facts.text: Eats out twice a week with his dinner club friends at a local chain restaurant; the food is fried and salty.
facts.say: Twice a week I go out with my dinner club. Old friends. The food's fried and salty, the good stuff.

facts.text: Orders the 'special' versions of menu items, which are higher in sodium.
facts.say: I always get the specials. Extra gravy, the works.

facts.text: Takes ibuprofen (Advil) 400 mg for back pain 2 to 3 times a week; does not know it can harm his heart and kidneys.
facts.say: Advil for my back. Two, three times a week. It's just Advil.

facts.text: Thinks his heart failure and diabetes are the same thing, his 'sick thing'.
facts.say: The sugar and the heart thing, it's all the same. My sick thing.

belief.text: Believes heart failure and diabetes are one illness.

facts.text: Drinks soda with every meal and avoids water; likes sweet tea and fruit punch.
facts.say: Soda with every meal. Sweet tea. Water's got no taste.

facts.text: Skips breakfast, eats his biggest meal at lunch around noon and snacks in the evening.
facts.say: I skip breakfast. Big lunch around noon, then I snack at night.

facts.text: Has no one to cook for him; relies on canned soups, instant mac and cheese and leftovers.
facts.say: Nobody cooks for me. Canned soup, the box mac and cheese, leftovers.

facts.text: Loves salty food and is skeptical of a low-sodium diet; canned soup is his comfort food.
facts.say: Low salt? Then what's the point of eating. Soup's my comfort food.

facts.text: Believes healthy eating is for the young, healthy and rich; food is about comfort and joy.
facts.say: Healthy eating's for young folks with money. Food's supposed to make you feel good.

facts.text: Has trouble getting up in the morning and getting to the grocery store.
facts.say: Mornings are rough. Getting to the store is a whole production.

facts.text: His sister lives across the country; he feels guilty that he is not taking care of himself and does not want to bother her.
facts.say: My sister's across the country. She worries, and I'm not exactly taking care of myself. I don't want to bother her.

facts.text: Widowed; lives alone in a two-bedroom apartment.
facts.say: It's just me in the apartment since my wife passed.

facts.text: Talks with a group of retired friends online; no in-person support at home.
facts.say: Got some retired buddies I talk to on Facebook.

facts.text: Retired janitor.
facts.say: Retired. Janitor, my whole working life.

facts.text: Skips metformin some days because it makes him nauseous and sometimes vomit.
facts.say: That metformin makes me throw up. Some days I just skip it.

facts.text: Takes lisinopril every morning; believes it is only for blood pressure.
facts.say: Lisinopril every morning. That one's for my pressure.

belief.text: Thinks lisinopril is only for blood pressure (it also treats his heart failure and protects his kidneys).

facts.text: Sometimes forgets eplerenone; worries it will drop his blood pressure and make him faint.
facts.say: The water pill, I forget that one sometimes. Scared it'll make me pass out.

facts.text: His medicines give him stomach upset and dizziness.
facts.say: The pills make me dizzy and mess with my stomach.

facts.text: Takes melatonin 5 mg at night.
facts.say: Melatonin at night, for sleep.

facts.text: Allergic to penicillin (hives), shellfish (anaphylaxis) and sulfa.
facts.say: Penicillin gives me hives. Shellfish closes up my throat. And sulfa.

facts.text: Drinks 1 to 2 small cups of beer at night while watching TV.
facts.say: A small beer or two in front of the TV.

facts.text: Has never smoked.
facts.say: Never smoked. Not once.

facts.text: Wakes up several times a night to urinate, which ruins his sleep.
facts.say: I'm up all night going to the bathroom. Can't get any sleep.

facts.text: Is very thirsty all the time.
facts.say: I'm thirsty all the time.

facts.text: Tired and short of breath with very little effort; sits most of the day.
facts.say: I get winded walking to the kitchen. Tired all the time.

facts.text: Has swelling in both ankles.
facts.say: My ankles swell up, both of them.

facts.text: Has sore, stiff joints.
facts.say: My joints are stiff and sore.

facts.text: Has lost weight without trying and is scared of losing muscle.
facts.say: I'm losing weight and I'm not even trying. Scares me. I'm getting weak.

facts.text: Used to be very active and is frustrated that he cannot do much now.
facts.say: I used to be on my feet all day. Now look at me.

facts.text: Is admitted to the hospital often for his heart.
facts.say: I'm in that hospital so much they know me by name.

facts.text: Thinks doctors keep him in the hospital to make money.
facts.say: They keep me in there so they can bill me.

facts.text: Had heart bypass surgery (CABG) 5 years ago.
facts.say: Had bypass surgery on my heart, five years back.

facts.text: Has had type 2 diabetes for 15 years.
facts.say: Diabetes, fifteen years now.

facts.text: His fixed income makes fresh food and medicines expensive.
facts.say: I'm on a fixed income. Fresh food costs money. So do the pills.

facts.text: Wants to stay out of the hospital and keep his independence.
facts.say: I want to stay out of that hospital. And keep doing for myself.

facts.text: Wants someone to explain exactly how his diabetes and heart failure are connected.
facts.say: If somebody would just explain how the sugar and the heart go together.

facts.text: Says he knows he should eat better but 'who cares', yet he does not want to die on the couch.
facts.say: I know, I know, eat better. Who cares. But I don't want to die on the couch either.

facts.text: Feels he failed his kids and his late wife; afraid he is a 'bad' person because he does not follow the diet.
facts.say: I wasn't the husband I should've been. Wasn't there for my kids. Now I can't even follow a diet.

facts.text: Is scared about his future and his health.
facts.say: Truth is, I'm scared. What happens to me when I can't do for myself?

facts.text: Has money in his checking account that he does not use because he is afraid of wasting it.
facts.say: I've got some money put away. I don't touch it. Scared I'll need it.

artifacts.title: Referral from primary care
artifacts.body: Medical nutrition therapy referral. 72-year-old man with uncontrolled type 2 diabetes (A1C 8.7%), heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (EF 40%), hypertension, chronic kidney disease stage 3 and coronary artery disease after bypass surgery. Frequent admissions for heart failure. Please assess diet, sodium and fluid habits and support medicine adherence.

diagnoses.name: Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (EF 40%)
Coronary artery disease, after bypass surgery (CABG)

codes.display: Atherosclerotic heart disease of native coronary artery without angina pectoris

objectives.text: Apply the Nutrition Care Process: find his eating pattern, beliefs and barriers.
Connect his medicines to nutrition care, including over-the-counter pain relievers.
Use motivational interviewing to explore what matters to him and how ready he is.
Write a PES statement supported by what you found.

actions.description: Explains that ibuprofen, Advil or other NSAIDs can worsen heart failure, raise blood pressure or hurt the kidneys, or suggests asking the doctor about a safer pain option
Discusses lowering salt or sodium, for example at the dinner club or with canned soup
Discusses swapping soda or sweet tea for water or unsweetened drinks

decision_points.label: Found the ibuprofen use and explained the risk
decision_points.feedback_if_yes: You found that Walter takes ibuprofen and explained why it is risky with heart failure and kidney disease.
decision_points.feedback_if_no: Walter takes ibuprofen for back pain. With heart failure and kidney disease that is a safety issue. Ask about over-the-counter pain medicine, then explain the risk in plain words.

decision_points.label: Agreed on a salt plan that fits his dinner club
decision_points.feedback_if_yes: You tied the salt advice to his real life: the dinner club.
decision_points.feedback_if_no: Walter eats out twice a week. Advice that ignores the dinner club is unlikely to stick.

decision_points.label: Checked his understanding (teach-back)
decision_points.feedback_if_no: Ask Walter to say the plan back in his own words.

branches.label: Stopped ibuprofen and changed dinner-club orders
branches.summary: He switched to Tylenol for his back and orders the plain version at the dinner club. Blood pressure and swelling are better.

add_facts.text: Switched to Tylenol for his back and asks for the plain version at the diner.
add_facts.say: I switched to Tylenol like you said. And I get the plain chicken at the diner now. Not bad.

branches.label: Stopped ibuprofen but same restaurant food
branches.summary: He stopped the ibuprofen, but dinner-club meals are the same. Swelling is about the same.

add_facts.text: Stopped the Advil, but still eats the same at the dinner club.
add_facts.say: I quit the Advil. The diner, well, that's the diner.

branches.label: Ibuprofen missed: hospitalized
branches.summary: Nobody caught the ibuprofen. Two weeks later he was hospitalized with fluid in his lungs and worse kidney function.

add_facts.text: Was in the hospital for 4 days with fluid in his lungs.
add_facts.say: Back in the hospital. Four days. Fluid in my lungs again.

add_facts.text: Still takes Advil for his back.
add_facts.say: Still taking the Advil. My back doesn't care about my heart.
